cottage.note: A cottage is a small, simple house, often in the country, not a big modern house.

ex: The maximum for this room is ten people.
You can stay for a maximum of three days.
Can I take a maximum of two bags?
Set the heat to the maximum, please.
maximum.note: Often used before a noun: "maximum speed", "maximum size".

ex: This phone has a new, faster chip.
There is a chip in your bank card.
This company makes chips for computers and cars.
Does your dog have a chip under its skin?
chip.note: Most often "chips" are thin fried potato slices: "a bag of chips."

ex: The bank is the main sponsor of the race.
Our team needs a new sponsor this year.
Who is the sponsor of this event?
The sponsors paid for the whole concert.
The activists marched to city hall.
She is an activist for clean air.
The police arrested several activists last night.
He became an animal rights activist after college.
The stock market index went up again today.
What is the UV index outside today?
The price index shows that food got more expensive.
Check your body mass index with this app.
index.note: Also the list at the back of a book. Plural: indexes (indices in science).

bowling.note: Say "go bowling" (not "go to bowling"): "Let's go bowling tonight."

ex: Oranges are full of vitamin C.
I take vitamins every morning with breakfast.
Where can I buy vitamins for kids?
In winter, many people need more vitamin D.
We reached a compromise after a long talk.
Both sides had to make a compromise.
Can we find a compromise on the price?
The new plan is a good compromise for everyone.
compromise.note: We say "reach a compromise" or "make a compromise".

ex: The country passed new laws against terrorism.
Terrorism is a danger to many big cities.
She studies the causes of terrorism in college.
The police called the attack an act of terrorism.
terrorism.note: Uncountable: no "a" and no plural (not "a terrorism").

supervisor.note: "Manager" or "boss" is more common in everyday speech.

ex: The next segment of the show is about food.
This phone is in the low-price segment.
Draw a line segment from A to B.
Our company wants to enter a new market segment.
The scandal brought the company a lot of bad publicity.
The new movie got a lot of publicity.
She hates publicity and rarely gives interviews.
Is this just a trick for publicity?
publicity.note: Uncountable: a lot of publicity (not "a publicity").

ex: How many siblings do you have?
I have two siblings, a brother and a sister.
Young siblings often fight over toys.
She is very close to her siblings.
sibling.note: Formal; in everyday speech people often say "brothers and sisters".

ex: The fans wore their team jerseys to the game.
He bought a soccer jersey with his favorite number.
After the game, the players swapped jerseys.
Does this jersey come in a smaller size?
jersey.note: Most often in the name "New Jersey" (a US state). As a word, usually a sports shirt.

ex: The police are investigating a kidnapping downtown.
The kidnapping shocked the whole town.
He went to prison for kidnapping a child.
The movie is about a kidnapping in a big city.
The cowboy rode his horse across the field.
He wore a cowboy hat and boots.
Cowboys work with cows and horses on big farms.
My son wants to be a cowboy for Halloween.
My daughter takes ballet lessons after school.
We saw a ballet at the theater last night.
She has danced ballet since she was five.
Are there any tickets for the ballet tonight?
ballet.note: Uncountable for the dance: "I love ballet." "A ballet" is one show: "We saw a ballet."

archive.note: Often used in the plural: the archives.

ex: Everything around us is made of atoms.
An atom is too small to see.
A water molecule has three atoms.
In class today, we learned about the atom.

appetite.note: Not a wish before meals: say "Enjoy your meal!" (not "Good appetite!").

ex: The film is still in production.
She works in TV production in Kyiv.
The production of the show took a year.
Our small video production company makes ads.
production.note: Most often "production" means making things: "car production", "food production".

visa.note: We say "apply for a visa" and "get a visa".

ex: The farmer keeps a shotgun to protect his chickens.
In this video game, the shotgun is very strong.
He went hunting for ducks with a shotgun.
Is it legal to own a shotgun here?
shotgun.note: Also informal "ride shotgun": sit in the front seat of a car.

escort.note: Often a verb: "Staff will escort you out." "An escort" can also mean a paid companion.

picnic.note: Say "have a picnic" or "go on a picnic".

ex: Our team is in the playoffs this year!
We watched the playoff game together at a bar.
They lost in the first round of the playoffs.
When do the playoffs start this year?
She paid me a nice compliment today.
Thank you so much for the compliment!
He often gives his wife compliments.
Is that a compliment or not?
compliment.note: Do not mix up with "complement" (something that goes well with another thing).

ex: The hotel offers a free airport transfer.
Can we book a transfer from the airport?
The player's transfer to a new club cost millions.
Our transfer to the hotel took about an hour.
transfer.note: Most often "transfer" means moving money or people: "a bank transfer", "transfer to a new school".

ex: The monument stands in the city square.
They built a monument to the soldiers.
Excuse me, how do I get to the monument?
Tourists take photos next to the monument.
I love reading fantasy books before bed.
This is a fantasy movie with dragons.
Do you like fantasy or science fiction more?
She writes fantasy stories for young readers.
fantasy.note: Most often a "fantasy" is something you imagine or dream about: "a childhood fantasy".

ex: The interior of the house is very modern.
I love the leather interior of your car.
She wants to study interior design in college.
The interior of the cafe is warm and cozy.
The coffee filters are in the top drawer.
We changed the water filter last week.
Can you add a filter to this photo?
The car needs a new oil filter.
Many people just want to keep the status quo.
The new boss wants to change the status quo.
She is not happy with the status quo at work.
Why should we accept the status quo?
status quo.note: Means "the way things are now". Usually with "the".

ex: Excuse me, what is the Wi-Fi password?
Does the hotel have free Wi-Fi?
The Wi-Fi in my room is very slow.
Connect your phone to the Wi-Fi first.
Wi-Fi.note: Uncountable: "free Wi-Fi" (not "a Wi-Fi"). Also written "WiFi" or "wifi".

ex: English is the de facto language of business.
He became the de facto leader of the team.
She is de facto the boss of this office.
Their parents are away, so Anna is de facto in charge.
de facto.note: Formal. Means "in real life" (not by law): "the de facto leader".

ex: We went on a cruise to the Caribbean.
How much does a ten-day cruise cost?
They met on a cruise ship last summer.
My parents want to take a river cruise.
cruise.note: Also a verb: "cruise" means drive or move at an easy, steady speed.

ex: Good evening, monsieur, welcome to our hotel.
The waiter asked, "Anything else, monsieur?"
Monsieur, your table by the window is ready.
Excuse me, monsieur, is this your bag?
monsieur.note: French word; used in English mainly to address a French man.

constable.note: British; in the US say "police officer".

ex: I have toast and eggs for breakfast.
She puts butter and jam on her toast.
Can you make me two slices of toast?
Oh no, the toast is burned again!
toast.note: Bread: some toast, two slices of toast (not "a toast"). "A toast" is a drink to someone.

propaganda.note: Uncountable. Always negative in English: one-sided information to change what people think.

ex: I left a message in the group chat.
We had a video chat with Grandma yesterday.
Can you add me to the class chat?
Write to us in the chat on our website.
chat.note: Most often a "chat" is a friendly talk: "Let's have a chat over coffee."

ex: World leaders met at a summit in Geneva.
The summit lasted for two long days.
Climate change was the main topic of the summit.
The next summit will take place in Kyiv.
summit.note: Also the top of a mountain: "We reached the summit at noon."

trader.note: Also someone who buys and sells goods: "a market trader".

ex: He was in a coma for three weeks.
The patient woke up from the coma.
The accident put her in a coma.
Doctors kept him in a coma so he could heal.
The congressman met with voters in our town.
She wrote a letter to her congressman.
The congressman voted against the new law.
He was elected congressman last year.
I play games on my PC at night.
My PC is very slow; can you help?
She bought a new PC for work.
Turn off the PC before you leave.
PC.note: Also "politically correct": "That joke is not PC."

ex: His grandfather was a communist all his life.
The communists took power after the war.
She was arrested for being a communist.
Many communists left the party after 1991.
communist.note: Often an adjective: "a communist country", "the Communist Party".
